source.citation: Lavergne, F., Ben Fraj, A., Bayane, I., Barthélémy, J.-F. (2018). Estimating the mechanical properties of hydrating blended cementitious materials: an investigation based on micromechanics. Cement and Concrete Research 104, 37-60.

transcription.from: the published article (PDF): Tables 3, 4, 7, 9 and 11, pp. 39, 41, 45 and 55, read on the page images and, for Table 7, on the text layer by column; the calorimeter of p. 51; Figs. 1, 4 to 7 and 9(b), pp. 42, 46 to 50 and 52, read exactly from their vector drawings; Figs. 15(a) and 16(a), p. 56, read from their raster image as described in the notes and in the digitization of their tables
transcription.note: The values were in src/kinetics/rate_models.jl before this file existed and agree with the article to the last digit. Table 3 gives the parameters of Parrott and Killoh (1984) as reported by Lothenbach et al. (2008), ref. [30] of the article. The text cites the activation energies of Table 4 to refs. [60, 64], [60] being Maekawa et al. (1999). The pozzolanic kinetics of p. 42, Eqs. (24)-(25), follow Waller (1999), ref. [31], with n and tau adjusted to the SEM analyses of ref. [81]. Table 9 and Table 11 (p. 55) and the calorimeter of p. 51 were in the scripts and pages before this file existed and agree with the article. Table 11 names one mix C75FA525 at w/b = 0.5 and C75FA25 at 0.32; both spellings are kept as printed.

T_ref.location: Table 3 caption, p. 39 (20 °C); also p. 42 for the pozzolanic reaction
T_ref.description: Temperature at which the kinetic parameters apply.

blaine_ref_clinker.description: Blaine fineness B0 for which the Parrott-Killoh adjustments are valid.

waller_n.description: Exponent of the sigmoid in log time of the degree of pozzolanic reaction of a fly ash.

waller_tau_fly_ash.description: Characteristic time of the pozzolanic reaction of a fly ash of 60 % pozzolanic activity.

waller_blaine_ref.description: Blaine fineness of the fly ash to which the pozzolanic kinetics refer.

waller_Ea.description: Activation energy of the pozzolanic reactions.

blaine_silica_fume.description: Blaine fineness taken by default for silica fume so that silica fume and fly ash share the same kinetics; a convention, not a measurement (the B.E.T. surface quoted on the same page is about 20 000 m^2/kg).

pozzolanic_activity_fly_ash.description: Pozzolanic activity of the fly ash assumed in the adjustment of the sigmoid.

blaine_limestone_filler.description: Blaine fineness of the limestone filler of the blends.

sand_water_absorption.description: Water absorbed by the dry sand, as a fraction of its mass; the water of Table 11 includes it, so that the paste is at the stated w/b.

calorimeter_heat_capacity.description: Heat capacity of the semi-adiabatic calorimeter, printed 'about 380 kJ/K'. The package reads the number as 380 J/K: see CALORIMETRY_VESSEL_CP in scripts/ionic_hydration.jl.

clinker_percent.description: Clinker in the CEM I 52.5 N of the study, percent by mass of cement.

gypsum_percent.description: Gypsum in the cement, percent by mass.

heat_loss_a.description: Linear coefficient of the calorimeter's heat loss, from its calibration to NF EN 196-9.

heat_loss_b.description: Quadratic coefficient of the calorimeter's heat loss; printed 0.260.

limestone_percent.description: CaCO3 in the cement, percent by mass.

bet_silica_fume.description: B.E.T. specific surface of silica fume, 'about 20,000 m2/kg', which the article quotes from its ref. [31], Waller (1999).

csh_water.location: Table 1, p. 38: the C-S-H C1.7SH4, saturated by the caption of Table 2, p. 39
csh_water.description: Moles of water per mole of silica of the C-S-H formed by the hydration of the clinker, its gel water included.

pozzolanic_csh_water.location: Table 1, p. 38, and Section 1.4, p. 41: the C-S-H C1.1SH3.9 of the pozzolanic reaction
pozzolanic_csh_water.description: Moles of water per mole of silica of the C-S-H formed by the pozzolanic reaction, its gel water included.

cement_bogue.location: Table 9, p. 55: the Bogue composition of the clinker, percent by mass of clinker

semi_adiabatic_limestone_wb050_temperatu.location: Fig. 15(a), p. 56: temperature of the limestone mortars of Table 11 at w/b = 0.5 in the semi-adiabatic calorimeter (thick lines), where the band of each is not covered by another; C95L05 is read near its maximum and from 1.1 to 1.4 days only, the rest of its band lying under those of C90L10 and C85L15; the crosses before about 0.6 d, which overlap between the mixes, are not transcribed

digitization.tool: the lines located by color (hue, saturation above 0.25) and told apart by stroke width, the thick measured bands followed column by column with sub-pixel edges; a band covered on one side by a color drawn after it read from its free edge, at half its median extent; overlaps otherwise left out; mapped through the placement of the image and the vector frame of the panel (0 to 5 days, 10 to 70 C)
digitization.note: One pixel is 0.14 K and 0.008 d. The colors are attributed from the vector legend, its rows matched in height to the line samples of the image: blue C100, green C95L05, yellow C90L10, orange C85L15, red C70L30, drawn in that order, each over the ones before. Each bin of 0.05 d holds the least-squares line of its readings evaluated at its center. The same reading of the C100 band agrees with semi_adiabatic_C100_wb050_temperature to 0.03 K in root mean square (0.12 K at most), which measures the reproducibility of the reading of one raster, not its accuracy.

semi_adiabatic_wb050_maximum.location: Figs. 15(a) and 16(a), p. 56: the maximum of the measured temperature of each mortar of Table 11 at w/b = 0.5 in the semi-adiabatic calorimeter, read where it is drawn (C100 from Fig. 15(a); C85SF15, whose record ends before its maximum, is left out); time_low and time_high bound the instants where the curve stays within one pixel (0.14 K) of its maximum, the uncertainty of the time

notes: The article writes the first author of the 1984 model 'Parrot'; the name is Parrott.
p. 42 prints 'E_S,A = 83,14 kJ/mol (E_S,A/R = 100 K)'; the ratio of the two is 1.0e4 K. Only the activation energy is kept here.
Table 11: the water accounts for the 0.9 % absorption of the dry sand; the w/b of C85L15 in the first group is 0.48 (asterisk in the table).

semi_adiabatic_C100_wb050_temperature is read from Fig. 15(a), which is a raster image (JPEG) under vector axes: the thick blue line of the measured C100 curve was located column by column by its color and its width, in image pixels mapped to the page through the placement of the image, and to time and temperature through the vector frame of the panel (0 to 5 days, 10 to 70 C). The points are averaged over 0.05 d. Before about 0.6 d the measured curve is drawn as crosses that overlap those of the other mixes, and after 3.5 d it lies under them: neither part is transcribed. One pixel is 0.03 K and 0.008 d; the width of the line makes the reading good to about 0.2 K.
